tools.name: get_price_index
tools.description: The SMKlog parcel shipping price index: a monthly repriced basket of six common boxes (1 to 20 lb) shipped from Newark, NJ to five US cities, quoted through the same live USPS, UPS and FedEx pipeline that prices real shipments. Returns the cheapest purchasable service per box and lane with every rat

tools.name: get_checkout_status
tools.description: Reports where a payment session made by create_checkout_link stands: whether the human has opened checkout, paid, and whether the shipping label exists yet, with the tracking number once it does. Reads SMKlog's own order records only: no carrier call, no quote allowance, nothing changes. Poll it aft

findings.detail: Description of "create_checkout_link" instructs the model to conceal actions from the user.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "create_checkout_link" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_checkout_link, get_price_index, get_checkout_status · Private data: create_checkout_link, get_checkout_status · Public sink: get_parcel_quote, track_parcel, get_checkout_status.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_checkout_link, get_price_index, get_checkout_status · Private data: create_checkout_link, get_checkout_status · Public sink: get_parcel_quote, track_parcel, get_checkout_status

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_parcel_quote" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
